newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds spurt higher on U.S. bond rally.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds spurt higher on U.S. bond rally.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose sharply Tuesday on the back of a surge in U.S. treasuries that came after a decline in the U.S. October consumer confidence index.
Traders said the drop in the U.S. 30-year bond yield to as low as 6.69 percent gave a large impetus to Argentine bonds, with Bradies benefitting the most.
The mainly locally traded dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.55 to 118.15.
Traders were cautiously optimistic that the volatility of recent sessions could subside if this turnaround in the market's trend is sustained.
Still, one trader said "it is difficult to sense a real turn in the trend." He pointed out that with the sharp rise in U.S. treasuries Tuesday they could well fall back down in coming sessions.

On the other hand, with more U.S. economic indicators due for release this week, including the important jobless report on Friday, there was scope for those figures to continue supporting the market, said market players.

Another trader said there was evidence of selling as well this session, when prices were at their highest levels of the day, indicating that some of the uncertainty of recent sessions was still intact.
Traders said once again there were no real investor flows in the market, with inter-bank trade dominating.
Separately, Argentina's industrial output rose 11.1 percent in September compared with the same month a year earlier, the Economy Ministry reported Tuesday.
In the money markets, call money fell 6.38 percent from 6.48 percent.
